subtitle: Integrated Math and Science for Architecture I
courseType:

keywords: Functions 2.Trigonometric functions 3.Exponential functions and logarithmic functions
educationalGoal: Students will learn: (1) basic functions and their graphs, and inverse functions (2) trigonometric functions (3) exponential functions and logarithmic functions
advice: This is a basic course in calculus for students in the Dept. of Architecture. We will cover the following topics: 1. Functions 2. Trigonometric functions 3. Exponential functions and logarithmic functions Extra classes may be held depending the comprehension level of students. Students are required to review and preview each class. As a matter of particular emphasis, students are required to attempt the exercises after each class. Extra materials may be distributed if necessary. Students are required to show their solution/calculation procedure logically and clearly in each assignment. Students are expected to utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center or the office hours of the teacher.
books: Textbooks:Integrated Math and Science for Architecture I II [Kanazawa Institute of Technology] Reference books:None Reserved books:None
requiredKnowledge: Basic calculation skills for numerical formulas (expansion, factorization, division, and calculation of fractional formula).

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the concept of a function and draw graphs of basic functions.
Be able to explain the concepts of trigonometric functions, exponential functions, and logarithmic functions.
Be able to explain various problems in architecture using elementary functions.
Be able to demonstrate an understanding of all topics, attend every class, and do all the necessary work.
Understand the meanings of fundamental English words for mathematics.
